questions.stem: Duct of Bellini are present in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Kidney
  • Papillary (collecting) ducts are anatomical structures of the kidneys, previously known as the ducts of Bellini.
  • Papillary ducts represent the most distal portion of the collecting duct.
  • They receive renal filtrate (precursor to urine) from several medullary collecting ducts and empty into a minor calyx.

Duct of Bellini




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No. 368,369,370.

questions.stemHtml: Marked area in the given Image is supplied by which dermatome?
questions.solutionHtml:
T10

Marked area is near the umbilicus and dermatome for this is T10.

A dermatome is an area of skin that is mainly supplied by afferent nerve fibers from a single nerve which form a part of a spinal nerve.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No.235.

questions.stem: What is the nerve supply of Submandibular gland:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lingual nerve

Parasympathetic innervation of submandibular gland originates from the superior salivatory nucleus through pre-synaptic fibres, which travel via the chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve (CNVII).

The chorda tympani then unifies with the lingual branch of the mandibular nerve (CNViii) before synapsing at the submandibular ganglion.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No. 148.

questions.stem: Structure derived from first pharyngeal arch:
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior belly of digastric
  • The anterior belly of the digastric and the mylohyoid nerve form from the first pharyngeal arch, also known as the mandibular arch.
  • The posterior belly of the digastric and the facial nerve derives from the second pharyngeal arch or the hyoid arch.

questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a boundary of Calot’s triangle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gallbladder
  • The triangular region formed between the cystic duct, the common hepatic duct and the inferior surface of the liver is the hepatobiliary triangle.
  • It is often mistakenly referred to as Calot’s triangle, which is an isosceles triangle based on the common hepatic duct, with the cystic artery and cystic duct forming its sides.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No. 338.

Right Aortic Sinus

Right coronary artery  arises from anterior aortic sinus also known as  Right aortic sinus.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 298.

questions.stem: Contralateral loss of pain and temperature is due to injury to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lateral spinothalamic tract
  • Damage to the lateral spinothalamic tract leads to loss of pain and temperature on the opposite side of the body below the level of lesion, since the neurons of this tract crosses to the opposite side in the spinal cord.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No. 45,46.

questions.stem: All of the following are extension of external oblique aponeurosis except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Linea semilunaris

Linea Semilunaris - It is a curved furrow, which extends from tip of the 9th costal cartilage to the pubic tubercle. It corresponds to the lateral margin of the rectus abdominis.

Linea Semilunaris

Liver
  • The perisinusoidal space (or space of Disse) is a location in the liver between a hepatocyte and a sinusoid.
  • It contains blood plasma.
  • Microvilli of hepatocytes extend into this space, allowing proteins and other plasma components from the sinusoids to be absorbed by the hepatocytes.

Space of Disse

Gitter cells:

  • These cells are macrophages and because of their appearance they are called “gitter cells”.
  • They look this way because they are lipid-laden.

Gitter cells

questions.stem: Parathyroid gland is implanted in which muscle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Brachioradialis

Parathyroid autotransplantation (PA) is an important technique for dealing with parathyroid glands removed in thyroidectomy and other neck surgeries. Unintentional parathyroidectomy is a major cause of postoperative hypoparathyroidism in total thyroidectomy with or without lymph node dissection.

Parathyroid surgery: Autotransplantation

  • Each parathyroid gland is sliced into 1–3 mm slices and three or four grafts were implanted into separated muscle pockets in the anterior forearm muscles (in brachioradialis muscle), then the muscle is closed with non-absorbable sutures.


Parathyroid transplantation in thyroid surgery Marcin Barczyński, 1 Filip Gołkowski,2 and Ireneusz Nawrot3.

questions.solutionHtml:
Right & Left liver lobe

Functional lobes of the liver

  • The functional right and left lobes of the liver are separated by an imaginary plane passing along the floor of fossa for gallbladder and the groove for inferior vena cava (cholecysto-Vena Caval line/ Cantlie’s plane).
  • On the anterosuperior surface of the liver, this plane passes from the IVC to the cystic notch present a little to the right of the falciform ligament.
  • The physiological right and left lobes are approximately equal in size.
  • Each Functional lobe of the liver has its own primary branch of the hepatic artery and portal vein and is drained by its own hepatic duct.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No.359,360.

questions.stem: Syndrome associated with posterior inferior cerebellar artery thrombosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
Wallenberg syndrome
  • Wallenberg syndrome is also known as lateral medullary syndrome or the posterior inferior cerebellar artery syndrome.
  • This neurological disorder is associated with a variety of symptoms that occur as a result of damage to the lateral segment of the medulla posterior to the inferior olivary nucleus.
  • It is the most typical posterior circulation ischemic stroke syndrome in clinical practice.
  • Etiology: It is caused most commonly by atherothrombotic occlusion of the vertebral artery, followed most frequently by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery, and least often, the medullary arteries.
  • Risk factor: Hypertension is the commonest risk factor followed by smoking and diabetes.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No. 106.

questions.stem: Which of the following exocrine glandular ducts are not obstructed in cystic fibrosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
Sweat gland

Abnormal Characteristics of Cystic fibrosis  Patients

  • The ducts of the mucus secreting glands are obstructed because of high viscosity of these secretions which leads to glandular dilatation and destruction.
  • The ducts of sweat glands are free from obstruction because the sweat gland has abnormal concentrations of inorganic ions, rather than glandular obstruction with thick mucus.


Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice 42nd, Page No.42.
